title: RAR: Retrieving And Ranking Augmented MLLMs for Visual Recognition

contributions.purpose: Understand why existing vision-language models fail on datasets with large or fine-grained vocabularies, motivating a new approach.
contributions.mechanism: Comparative empirical analysis of CLIP and MLLMs, showing CLIP fails on fine-grained categories (language ambiguity/synonyms) while MLLM accuracy degrades as the number of candidate categories grows beyond the context window.
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative/motivational: on classification datasets (RAF-DB, DTD, Food101) CLIP is weak on fine-grained items while MLLMs (LLaVA) degrade under large vocabularies (Fig. 1).
contributions.source_quote: (1) We conduct an in-depth analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of VLMs and MLLMs in processing fine-grained datasets.

contributions.purpose: Enhance the few-shot/zero-shot fine-grained recognition ability of MLLMs on datasets with extensive vocabularies without losing their broad knowledge.
contributions.mechanism: RAR: a CLIP-based multi-modal retriever builds an explicit memory of categories beyond the context window; at inference the top-k similar candidates are retrieved and the MLLM ranks them to make the final prediction; a plug-and-play pipeline usable with various MLLMs, with ~30k fine-tuning data from FGVC-Aircraft to boost ranking.
contributions.evaluation: 5 fine-grained recognition benchmarks, 11 few-shot image recognition datasets, and 2 object detection datasets; few-shot avg accuracy over 11 datasets improves from CLIP+k-NN 63.2 to RAR 69.8 (4-shot); frozen CLIP ViT-B/16, k=5.
contributions.source_quote: (2) To enhance the fine-grained few-shot and zero-shot perception capabilities of MLLMs, we introduce RAR with a multi-modal retriever and the inference pipeline based on retrieving and ranking.(3) Our RAR can be seamlessly integrated into various MLLMs in a plug-and-play manner.

contributions.purpose: Verify that RAR improves visual recognition across a broad set of recognition tasks.
contributions.mechanism: Benchmarking RAR against CLIP and MLLM baselines on classification and object detection tasks.
contributions.evaluation: Across 11 classification datasets and 2 object detection datasets (LVIS, V3Det), RAR outperforms baselines; improved zero-shot detection AP over CLIP.
contributions.source_quote: (4) Through rigorous testing across 11 classification datasets and 2 object detection datasets, we demonstrate that our method outperforms baselines on a variety of visual recognition tasks.

self_declared_provenance.quote: To address these challenges, we propose augmenting standard MLLMs with our RAR, a retrieving-and-ranking augmented technique. Our RAR enables models to dynamically incorporate external knowledge into the processing and generation workflows.
We initially establish a multi-modal retriever based on CLIP to create and store explicit memory for different categories beyond the immediate context window.

notes: Reject paper. Results reported are all positive (few-shot accuracy 63.2->69.8, improved detection AP); no negative or tie results highlighted. PDF is the rebuttal version (states 'The new material added for the rebuttal discussion is in red'). Contributions are largely an integration of CLIP retrieval + MLLM ranking rather than a new model.
